chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: How head arrangements set the band's style
summary: Their style came from head arrangements built at rehearsal, with numbers lasting up to 30 minutes and a rhythm section building choruses before the horns entered.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, who sort of decided the style of your band?

Well, I'll tell you, the style was set this way. We did -- you know, we had a lot of music. But besides having a lot of music, we had twice that many head arrangements. Our style was set with head arrangements, with head arrangements, things that's done on the stand, at rehearsal, and the guys, they -- well, young. They could remember. They could remember. If we said, 'We're going to do it this way,' we did it that way.
And then -- it's just like we had numbers that could last ten, 15, 20, 30 minutes, the way we did them. One that last 30 minutes, we knew exactly what to do. We knew just --
We knew where we was going and we knew when we was going to get out of there, you know what I mean?

And that was the main thing. See, if we decided -- we start -- a lot of time, especially with rhythm section particularly, drum, bass, piano and guitar, we would just start. One chorus, second chorus, the cats want to come in, keep them out of the third chorus.
By the time we get to the fourth chorus, man, they raring to go, you know, they're raring to go, because see, we still trying to build, too.
And by the time then we turn them in and I just give them that, they there.

'Pee-Bo-Pent-Bo', (singing.) See, they ready to go, see. So then it was decided we're going to get in the bus, you know. 'Let's get in the bus.' Okay. Everybody starts setting it down. But everybody's got a job, see.

Bird going to set the riffs in the reed section, [Bob Gould] Buddy and Piggy going to set the riffs in the brass section, and when -- and the bones, you know what I mean. Sometimes got to have one bone, to have one bone, he'd have to go with the brass. If I had two bones, then they could work together. But they was -- either alternate, do it one way or the other. So consequently, we played so many head arrangements. That's where it was set. But we just sit and start playing, the rhythm section.
